title: React
subtitle: React builds the Mattermost plugins, the Teams work tab and the meeting-stage app for Helix.
lede: In Helix I wanted people, and the AI colleague they work with, to stay inside the platforms they already use. I build front ends as integration surfaces inside other people's platforms: small, native-looking and backed by a server-side source of truth. The Control Center, Helix's multi-model collaboration shell, runs on an unmodified Mattermost server. I extend it only through its supported plugin model: everything Helix adds to its interface is a Mattermost webapp plugin in React and JSX, and the plugins are thin. In Teams, the working service has a tab built with React and Microsoft's Fluent UI, so it looks native where it appears.
quote: Where a vendor feature has no control an agent can use, I build a surface I control.
evidence: Microsoft Teams app development: a Fluent UI work tab with Teams single sign-on, and a meeting-stage app an AI agent drives with each action bound to tenant, employee and meeting.
Mattermost plugin development: React webapp plugins for a multi-model collaboration shell, kept thin over server-side state in Rust and PostgreSQL.
author: Corey James
